requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The generator emits formatters for a type from a referenced assembly. A context-free reviewer would see this as contradicting the deliberate rule that referenced-assembly types get no formatter from the compiling assembly. L11 covers only the implicit TypeCollector path and is not a defect there. This is an explicit opt-in via [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter], and the requirement asks for it, so it is consistent.

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: Contractless mode skips public get-only properties and readonly fields, and constructor parameters are not matched. This differs from ContractlessStandardResolver, but L19 says to follow the requirement, and the requirement only says public members are in scope.
Receipts/GeneratedFormatterRequirementTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 2/2 failed
Receipts/GeneratedFormatterMetadataTypeTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 1/1 failed

Mutation: 11 killed, 3 survived, 3 compile errors, 0 timeouts (17 mutants on MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs, GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs, ObjectSerializationInfo.cs, GeneratorUtilities.cs, MessagePackGenerator.cs)

findings.claim: The data-type check rejects any T where `type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty`. A type that comes from a referenced assembly through a metadata (DLL) reference has no declaring syntax references. So the case the requirement exists for (ProjectA.MyType compiled into a referenced DLL, formatter declared in Project B) gets MsgPack021 and no generated formatter. The annotated class keeps no implementation, and the build fails with CS0535. Only same-compilation types, or types reached through CompilationReference, ever pass this check.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterRequirementTests.FormatterForTypeInReferencedAssemblyWithoutMessagePack_IsGenerated. It compiles ProjectA without MessagePack, emits it to an image and references it via MetadataReference.CreateFromImage. Expect it to fail on head with an MsgPack021 generator diagnostic and no 'partial class MyObjectFormatter' in the generated sources.

findings.claim: The acceptance criteria say that if T carries MessagePack attributes ([MessagePackObject]/[Key], or [DataContract]/[DataMember]) they are honoured, and that contractless mode applies only when those attributes are absent. With no surrogate, the collector always calls CreateContractlessMembers. That path never inspects T's attributes, so any T is serialized as public read-write members keyed by name. Keys, Order/Name, IgnoreMember and DataContract opt-in membership are all ignored, and members that T excludes are still serialized.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterRequirementTests.FormatterHonoursDataContractOnFormattedType. T is a [DataContract] type with one [DataMember(Order = 0)] property and one unannotated 'Secret' property. Expect head to fail because the generated formatter references 'Secret'.

findings.claim: The core scenario is rejected. The data-type guard includes `|| type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty`. Any `T` loaded from a compiled referenced assembly (a real metadata reference such as Project A's DLL) has no declaring syntax references. So `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.MyType>` reports MsgPack021 ('only accessible, non-generic, non-abstract classes and structs are supported') and emits no formatter body. The user's class then fails with CS0535. Only `T` declared in source in the same compilation (or reached through an in-memory CompilationReference) works, which contradicts the acceptance criterion 'even when T is declared in a referenced assembly'.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterMetadataTypeTests.FormatterForTypeFromCompiledReferencedAssembly_IsGenerated. It emits ProjectA to a PE image, references it via MetadataReference.CreateFromImage, and runs MessagePackGenerator. On head the generator reports MsgPack021 and the output compilation has CS0535 errors.

findings.claim: the change's tests do not detect swap-boolean at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Analyzers/MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:324
the change's tests do not detect negate-condition at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/ObjectSerializationInfo.cs:168
the change's tests do not detect delete-statement at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/MessagePackGenerator.cs:74

hunches.claim: The contractless wire contract excludes get-only properties and readonly fields, and members are ordered alphabetically. This differs from ContractlessStandardResolver, which includes more members and uses a different order. The same type formatted through the dynamic contractless resolver and through the generated formatter would produce different bytes or lose members. This is a new opt-in feature, so existing users are not affected. The ledger says to follow the requirement (L19).

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize a class with a get-only property and a public field using ContractlessStandardResolver and the generated formatter, then compare bytes.

hunches.claim: The attribute filter in GeneratorUtilities compares the display string of the attribute class against the full attribute name. It excludes formatters that carry [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] from hand-written formatter registration. Existing user formatters are unaffected, since the attribute is new.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun generator snapshot tests to confirm that existing outputs are unchanged.

hunches.claim: The requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes (DataContract or MessagePackObject), they are honoured. The collector ignores [MessagePackObject], [Key] and [DataMember] on T and always uses contractless members or the surrogate. A T annotated with [Key] therefore gets contractless output.

receipt_plan.detail: In the ExecutionTests, add an external-style type with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)] members, then generate a formatter for it with no surrogate. Assert that the output is an array with integer keys. The current code emits a string-key map.

hunches.claim: The `type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty` check rejects metadata-only types. That is the exact requirement scenario (T in a referenced assembly), and it would make the feature fail with MsgPack021. The execution tests may not exercise this path because ExternalTypes is a ProjectReference, which is still metadata-only for the consumer, so the tests pass only if the guard does not trigger. No Tests-project case covers a metadata type, and none covers a rejected source-less type.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:73 remove-guard: `|| type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty` -> deleted; expected to survive because no test in GeneratedMessagePackFormatterTests uses a metadata-only type, and the execution tests pass either way if the guard is a no-op.

hunches.claim: Contractless member ordering and the IsPublicReadWrite filter are only weakly tested. No test covers public fields, get-only/private-setter exclusion beyond one `Doubled` property, or inherited members. Removing the OrderBy or the base-type walk in GetInstanceMembers would not fail any test.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:226 delete-statement: `current = current.BaseType` loop advance -> removed so base members are skipped; expected to survive because no external test type has a base class with members.

hunches.claim: The honoring of MessagePack attributes on T (`[MessagePackObject]`/`[Key]`) is an acceptance criterion, but no test covers a T that carries attributes. Collect always uses contractless or surrogate members and ignores T's own attributes.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] for a type with [MessagePackObject]/[Key(5)] members and assert key 5 is emitted; expected to fail on head.

hunches.claim: The new diagnostics MsgPack019-022 are not added to AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md. Several diagnostic paths have no test: duplicate keys (KeysMustBeUnique), missing [Key] on a surrogate member, a class without a parameterless constructor, and the inaccessible type case. The diagnostic tests also hand-write the Members, so they do not prove that the generator emits no output for a rejected formatter.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:~178 negate-condition: `if (!claimedKeys.Add(key))` -> `if (claimedKeys.Add(key))`; expected to survive because there is no duplicate-key test.

hunches.claim: The surrogate test only checks the array length (8) and a round trip. It never asserts that the values sit at keys 3 and 7. It would not notice if the keys were mapped incorrectly, e.g. the `CreateMember(target, intKey: intKey ...)` swapped for the position index, as long as the round trip stayed symmetric.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:166 swap: `CreateMember(target, intKey: intKey, ...)` -> `intKey: members.Count`; expected to survive only partly, since the header length would then change to 2 and the array-length assertion would catch it. Value placement at keys 3 and 7 is still unasserted.

hunches.claim: MessagePack attributes on `T` are never honoured. When no surrogate is given, `CreateContractlessMembers` always serializes every public read-write member by name. It ignores `[MessagePackObject]`/`[Key]` int keys and `[IgnoreMember]` (and `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember]`/`[IgnoreDataMember]`) declared on `T`. Example: `T` has `[MessagePackObject] class T { [Key(0)] public int A {get;set;} [IgnoreMember] public int B {get;set;} }`. The generated formatter writes a string-keyed map containing both A and B, instead of an int-keyed array containing only A. This violates the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured.'

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect lines 88-96: the `surrogate is null` branch calls CreateContractlessMembers(type), which uses only IsPublicReadWrite and never inspects referenceSymbols.KeyAttribute or IgnoreAttribute on `type`'s members. Confirm with a generator run where T carries [Key]/[IgnoreMember] and inspect the generated formatter for an ignored member name and string keys.

hunches.claim: The new analyzer descriptors MsgPack019-022 are Error severity and enabled by default, but the diff does not show AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md being updated. This risks RS2000 release-tracking warnings in the analyzer build, and the rules are missing from the documented rule table. The diagnostics are only emitted for [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] users, so they do not affect existing users.

receipt_plan.detail: Check whether AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md has entries for MsgPack019-022 and whether build emits RS2000 under warnings-as-errors.

hunches.claim: Contractless mode serializes only public read-write members and requires a parameterless constructor, but the generated deserializer does not run MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep or UntrustedData handling differently from existing templates; no new weakening is visible. However the generated formatter for a partial class that the user declares as non-internal emits `partial class` without modifiers, which cannot conflict. No concrete security regression found in the diff.

receipt_plan.detail: Read the existing FormatterTemplate/StringKeyFormatterTemplate: they call options.Security.DepthStep(ref reader) before deserialization; the diff only changes the class declaration header, so the depth protection is retained.

hunches.claim: The new public attribute GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute in MessagePack.Annotations has no PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt entry shown in the diff. This is a convention violation if the repo tracks the public API surface.

receipt_plan.detail: Check src/MessagePack.Annotations/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt, if present, for the GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute entries.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Contractless by default, plus an optional SurrogateType for keys. Attributes on T are not read, and the surrogate type must be in the consuming assembly.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Contractless by default, but honour the attributes already on T ([MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[DataContract]). Drop the surrogate, or keep it only as an extra. This requires reading T's attributes in GeneratedFormatterCollector and choosing int or string keys from them.
